A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same information-theoretic regularizer. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and supplementary materials are readable and support comparison, including content moved between sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original compression experiments, out-of-domain evaluations, sensitivity and alignment studies, training-time measurements, and supplementary baseline reproductions.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations using ELIC and MLIC++, including compression, generalization, and training-time results.

M1.justification: The regularization loss and alternating training principle remain unchanged. V3 adds source-model adaptations using checkerboard and channel-sliced contexts for ELIC and attention-based contexts for MLIC++ (Figure 3), extending the architecture choices within the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions train on Flickr20k and evaluate on Kodak, Tecnick, CLIC, pixel-style images, SCI1K, CCT-CGI, and BRACS. Reported subset changes concern evaluation settings. V3's crater-exclusion footnote does not remove coverage evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: V3 adds matched unregularized ELIC and MLIC++ anchors alongside their regularized versions in the compression and generalization comparisons. V1 evaluates only hyperprior, autoregressive, and attention models; the supplementary comparison against pretrained CompressAI models is retained.

E3.justification: The added ELIC/MLIC++ experiments introduce mixed AUN-STE quantization, one million training steps, batch size 8, and source-model learning rate 10^-4, versus the retained classic-model settings of two million steps, batch size 16, and 10^-3. SCI1K selection changes from the first 100 test images to training images; BRACS changes from 100 test images to 81 specified images. These are reported setting changes, without establishing reruns.

E4.justification: V3 extends the existing out-of-domain robustness comparison to ELIC and MLIC++ in Table 1. The regularization-strength study, extended hyperprior training, and stronger/weaker source-model alignment tests already exist in v1; their consolidation into Figure 6 is a presentation change.

E5.justification: Both versions fix the training seed to 1. Neither reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, significance tests, or statistical error bars; the plotted dataset curves are not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V3 adds ELIC/MLIC++ results, including natural-image average BD-rates of -1.56% and -3.03%. Reported autoregressive averages change from -0.92% to -1.06%, and Kodak results from -1.15% to -1.57%. Training overheads change from 19.5%/11.3%/1.5% to 28.8%/18.2%/8.1% for the three retained models. However, Figure 4(b) retains autoregressive endpoints inconsistent with the revised text and Table 1.

T1.justification: The entropy lemmas, theorems, and supplementary proofs are substantively unchanged. V3 adds a simplified complexity derivation in Equation (17), assuming approximately equal source- and latent-model costs and expressing overhead through the transform-to-entropy-model complexity ratio.

C1.justification: The abstract and central compression/generalization claims remain unchanged. V3 narrows the concluding efficiency claim by dropping v1's explicit assertion of negligible training overhead for sufficiently complex backbones, while retaining the no-inference-overhead claim.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 adds arguments that the simplified regularizer constrains noisy gradients and that the omitted conditional-entropy gap should shrink during training. V3 also acknowledges exceptions to bitrate reduction and expands the discussion of architecture-dependent training overhead and possible mitigations in Section 4.3.

D1.justification: V3 supplies detailed ELIC/MLIC++ source architectures and module specifications, implementation provenance including an ELIC code reference, and their training settings. It also identifies the BRACS subfolder, specifies a 100,000-step timing measurement, and explicitly includes another source-model forward pass in Algorithm 1. Previously documented classic-model details are largely retained or relocated.

R1.justification: V3 replaces the MLIC citation with the distinct MLIC++ work and adds references for ELIC, its implementation, few-shot domain adaptation, and depthwise separable convolutions. The central positioning relative to quantization optimization and VAE regularization remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 substantially reorganizes the experimental narrative: source-model specifications and alignment analysis move from the supplement into the main text, min-max training receives expanded explanation, and a dedicated limitations subsection replaces the shorter complexity discussion. The supplement is reorganized around proofs, baseline reproduction, and module details.

P2.justification: V3 expands the training plots from three to five models, adds a second Kodak RD panel, enlarges Tables 1 and 2, and introduces expanded architecture diagrams. It combines the sensitivity and alignment plots into Figure 6, relocates existing supplementary displays, and substantially reformats the author block and page layout.

improvement.justification: The ELIC/MLIC++ evaluations strengthen support for applicability to advanced compression architectures, while fuller implementation details and training-cost analysis improve reproducibility and transparency. These gains support a modest net improvement. The unresolved disagreement between revised autoregressive results in Table 1 and the retained Figure 4(b) limits confidence in the numerical reporting.
